message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a **Google Compute Engine** instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and boots from the official Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image.

> ⚠️ **Note** – “EC2” is Amazon‑AWS terminology. In Google Cloud the equivalent service is **Compute Engine**.  
> Make sure you have:
> * A Google Cloud project (`PROJECT_ID`) with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * `gcloud` installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI command

```bash
# Set your project and zone first
export PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
export ZONE="us-central1-a"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
    --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
    --boot-disk-size=200GB \                # size of the OS disk
    --boot-disk-type=pd-balanced \          # SSD persistent disk
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \        # Ubuntu 20.04 LTS family
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \       # official Ubuntu image project
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \          # keep running during maintenance
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \   # full access
    --tags=http-server,https-server \       # allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic
    --metadata=startup-script='#!/bin/bash
        apt-get update && apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
        systemctl restart google-guest-agent' \   # optional: install GPU driver
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \   # add one RTX A6000
    --no-restart-on-failure
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | Size & performance of the OS disk. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu project. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000` is the internal code for RTX A6000. |
| `--metadata=startup-script` | Optional script that runs at boot (here we install the NVIDIA driver). |

> 📌 **Tip** – If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, adjust `count=` and `--machine-type`.  
> For example, `--machine-type=n1-highmem-32` gives 32 vCPUs & 124 GB RAM.

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to use the raw REST API, here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine Instances endpoint:

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-balanced"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": { "items": ["http-server", "https-server"] },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsystemctl restart google-guest-agent"
      }
    ]
  },
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ]
}
```

### How to POST it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances"
```

Replace `${PROJECT_ID}` and `${ZONE}` with your values. Save the JSON above to `instance.json`.

---

## 3️⃣  Verify the instance

After creation, check that the GPU is visible:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh my-rtx-a6000 --command="nvidia-smi"
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

## 4️⃣  Clean up

When you’re done, delete the instance to avoid ongoing charges:

```bash
gcloud compute instances delete my-rtx-a6000 --project=${PROJECT_ID} --zone=${ZONE}
```

---

### Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Project & billing enabled |
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | `gcloud` authenticated |
| ✅ | Correct machine type & GPU count |
| ✅ | Proper image family (`ubuntu-2004-lts`) |
| ✅ | GPU driver installed (via startup‑script or manually later) |
| ✅ | Firewall rules allow SSH (or open ports you need) |

That’s all you need to spin up a Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS!
